row.title: Appliance Repair
row.blurb: A visit to work out what is wrong with one appliance, and a written explanation of what repairing it would involve. Parts and the repair itself are quoted afterwards, so you decide once the fault is known.

page.title: Appliance Diagnostics — Book a Fault Assessment | Helpward
page.h1: Book an appliance diagnostic visit
page.intro: Something has stopped working and you do not yet know why. This booking buys the finding out: a helper comes, assesses the fault and explains it. On Helpward it is the Appliance Repair service, and what it delivers is a diagnosis — any actual repair is quoted afterwards and is yours to accept or refuse.

faqs.q: Is the repair included in this price?
faqs.a: No, and this is the thing worth reading twice. You are booking an assessment: the visit, the diagnosis and an explanation of what is wrong. Parts and labour to fix it are quoted separately once somebody has actually looked at it.

faqs.q: Which appliances can you assess?
faqs.a: Ordinary household machines — washers, dryers, dishwashers, fridges, ovens. The form asks which appliance, its make and model, and what it is doing, so a helper can tell before accepting whether it is something they know.

faqs.q: What model details do you need?
faqs.a: Make, model, and the symptom in your own words. An error code, if the machine shows one, is worth more than a paragraph of description.

faqs.q: How are parts and further work quoted?
faqs.a: By the helper, after the visit, as a separate arrangement. Helpward's booking covers the assessment; it is not a price cap on a repair and does not commit you to one.

faqs.q: Can I decline the repair quote?
faqs.a: Yes, with nothing further owed. You have paid for the diagnosis and the diagnosis is yours — take it to whoever you like.

faqs.q: Where is the appliance, and can it be moved?
faqs.a: The form asks, because a built-in oven and a freestanding one are different problems. Say whether it can be pulled out and whether there is room to work behind it.

includes: A visit to assess the fault
A plain explanation of what is wrong
A quote for the repair, which is yours to accept or refuse
excludes: The repair itself — it is quoted separately after the visit
Parts, which are not supplied under this booking
Gas, sealed-refrigerant or certified electrical work
Any guarantee the fault can be fixed

Know that this booking buys the diagnosis. Parts and repair are quoted afterwards, and you can decline.
Do not run the appliance just before the visit if it is leaking or tripping power.

row.title: Car Battery Jump
row.blurb: A roadside helper arrives with cables and a portable jump pack to start your dead battery — no tow needed.

page.title: Car Jump-Start Service — Dead Battery Help | Helpward
page.h1: Request a car jump-start for a dead battery
page.intro: A flat battery, someone there with cables and a portable jump pack, and no tow truck. On Helpward this is booked as the Car Battery Jump service: say where the car is and a nearby helper comes out to try to start it.

faqs.q: Can you jump-start my car where it is parked?
faqs.a: Usually, and the form asks where the car is precisely so a helper can judge that before accepting. Tell us the parkade level, the street or the driveway, and whether a second car can pull alongside — a battery that cannot be reached by another vehicle is the one case that tends to defeat a jump pack.

faqs.q: What vehicle details do you need?
faqs.a: Make and model, and where the battery sits — engine bay, boot, or under a seat. "Not sure" is an option; the helper brings leads for the common cases either way.

faqs.q: What if the battery will not start?
faqs.a: Then it will not start. This is an attempt by someone with cables and a jump pack, not a guaranteed repair: a battery that has failed outright, or a fault that is not the battery, needs a garage or a tow. You are paying for the visit and the attempt, and if something goes wrong with how it was handled you have 24 hours to open a dispute.

faqs.q: Is a replacement battery included?
faqs.a: No. The service is a jump-start. No part is supplied, fitted or sold as part of it.

faqs.q: How is the final price shown?
faqs.a: It is a flat price for the visit, plus the usual {fee} service fee, and it does not change with distance or how long the attempt takes. You see the whole figure before the request reaches a helper.

includes: A helper with jump leads and a portable jump pack
An attempt to start the car where it is parked
Batteries in the engine bay, boot or under a seat
excludes: A replacement battery, or any part supplied or fitted
Any guarantee the car will start
Towing, recovery or garage work
A battery no second vehicle or pack can reach

publicCopy.relatedPrompt: Dead battery instead?

items: Say exactly where the car is parked, and whether a second vehicle can pull alongside it.
Know your make and model, and where the battery sits — engine bay, boot, or under a seat. "Not sure" is a fine answer.
Make sure the car is reachable: unlocked, or with someone there to open it.
Switch everything off — lights, heater, radio — before the helper arrives.

intake.intro: So your helper brings the right leads and finds the car.

fields.label: Where is the car parked?
fields.hint: Parkade level, street, driveway — and whether a second car can pull alongside.

page.title: Platonic Date Companion — Book a Dinner Plus-One | Helpward
page.h1: Book a platonic plus-one for dinner or an occasion
page.intro: A plus-one for a dinner or an occasion where turning up alone is the awkward part. On Helpward this is the Date Companion service: one person, accompanying you, for the hours you book. The name describes the occasion, not the relationship — it is platonic.

faqs.q: Is this a romantic or sexual service?
faqs.a: No, and this is not a soft boundary. It is accompaniment and conversation in public, nothing else, ever. Any approach otherwise ends the booking and the account.

faqs.q: Can I book a dinner plus-one?
faqs.a: Yes — that is the central case. {base} covers the first {inclTime}, with {blockPrice} per extra minutes, so book through to when the evening actually ends.

faqs.q: Are food and event costs included?
faqs.a: No. The booking buys time. Dinner, drinks, entry and transport are separate, and worth settling in advance so neither of you is working it out at the table.

faqs.q: Can I specify a dress code?
faqs.a: Yes, and you should if the venue has one. Put it in the booking rather than mentioning it on the night.

faqs.q: Where does the booking begin and end?
faqs.a: At the public meeting point and the time you agreed, and it ends when the booked hours do. Nobody is obliged to continue past it and nobody should be asked to.

includes: One platonic companion for a dinner or occasion
A dress code and plan you set in the booking
The hours you book, from an agreed public meeting point
excludes: Anything romantic or sexual, without exception
Food, drink, entry or transport costs
Private residences as a meeting point
Continuing past the hours booked

row.title: Designated Driver
row.blurb: A licensed driver meets you and drives YOUR car home — ideal after drinks, late nights or long days.

page.title: Designated Driver — Get You & Your Car Home | Helpward
page.h1: Hire a designated driver to drive your car home
page.intro: A taxi brings its own car, which leaves yours where you left it. This is the other way round: a driver comes to you and drives your own car, with you in it, to wherever you are going. On Helpward it is the Designated Driver service.

faqs.q: Will the driver drive my own car?
faqs.a: Yes — that is the whole point of it. You travel as a passenger in your own vehicle, and the car ends up wherever you do. If you want a car supplied for you, that is a taxi, not this.

faqs.q: Can I book after drinking?
faqs.a: Yes. Getting home without driving yourself is the most common reason people book it. You are the passenger; nothing about the booking asks you to drive.

faqs.q: Can I request a driver for a manual car?
faqs.a: The booking form asks whether your car is automatic or manual, so a helper knows which they are accepting before they accept it. Say manual if it is manual — the request then only suits a driver who can drive one.

faqs.q: How is the trip price calculated?
faqs.a: By time booked, not by distance. The base price covers a set stretch of driving time and longer trips add whole blocks on top. Distance does not enter the figure at all, and the full total is on screen before the request goes anywhere.

faqs.q: Can I schedule a pickup?
faqs.a: Yes. A request can be for now or for a time you choose, which is the sensible way to book an evening out before the evening starts.

faqs.q: What vehicle details do you need?
faqs.a: Transmission, make and model, how many passengers are travelling, and exactly where the car is — a parkade level is not a street address. Every one of those is a question on the form, and the helper reads your answers before deciding to accept.

includes: A driver who comes to you and drives your own car
You and your passengers travelling in your own vehicle
Automatic or manual, whichever you tell us on the form
Booked now or scheduled for a time you choose
excludes: A car supplied for you — that is a taxi, not this
Driving anyone who is not travelling with you
Long-distance trips outside the areas we cover

publicCopy.relatedPrompt: Had a drink, with your own car to get home?

items: Have your keys and the car where you said it would be — a parkade level is not a street address.
Know whether the car is automatic or manual, and say so on the form. A manual needs a driver who can drive one.
Make sure the car is legal to drive: insured, registered, and with enough fuel for the trip.
Count your passengers before booking. Everyone travelling has to fit, belted, in your own car.

intake.intro: Your helper drives your car, so they need the route and the vehicle.

fields.label: Where to?
fields.hint: The drop-off address. Shared with your helper once they accept.

page.title: Dog Walking — Book a Local Dog Walker | Helpward
page.h1: Book a dog walker for your dog's next walk
page.intro: Your dog gets out, on a day you cannot take them. On Helpward this is the Dog Walking service: pick 30 or 60 minutes, say how many dogs are going, and the walker sends a photo update and a GPS-tracked route when they are done.

faqs.q: How long can I book a walk?
faqs.a: {base} covers the first {inclTime}, and longer walks add {blockPrice} per extra {blockTime}. A longer walk adds whole blocks rather than part of one, because a walker's time is booked rather than clocked.

faqs.q: Can I book more than one dog?
faqs.a: Yes. One dog is included and each additional dog is {unitPrice}. The form asks how many are going so the walker knows what they are agreeing to — three dogs on three leads is a different walk from one.

faqs.q: What should I leave for the walker?
faqs.a: A lead, fresh water, and treats if your dog has them. Leave anything the walker needs where you say it will be, and say where that is in the handover instructions.

faqs.q: How do I share access instructions?
faqs.a: Through the handover instructions on the booking. They are saved with the booking rather than sent in a message, and only the helper actually booked for the job can read them — not every walker who was offered it.

faqs.q: Will I receive an update?
faqs.a: Yes — a photo update and the route taken, which is the part most people book this for. You can also message the walker while the walk is on.

faqs.q: Can I book the same walker again?
faqs.a: Yes. A walker you have used before can be saved as a favourite, and new requests can be routed to them first rather than to whoever is nearest.

page.title: Senior Companionship — Everyday Help for Older Adults | Helpward
page.h1: Book companionship and everyday help for an older adult
page.intro: Company, and a hand with the ordinary things — grocery trips, doctor visits, conversation, light housekeeping. On Helpward this is the Elder Assistance service, booked by the hour for a parent or grandparent, or for yourself. It is companionship and practical help, not care.

faqs.q: Is this medical or personal care?
faqs.a: No. No medication is given or managed, no personal or intimate care, no nursing, no clinical task of any kind. Helpers are approved by a person at Helpward, not licensed care professionals, and anything in that territory needs a home-care provider instead.

faqs.q: Can I book for a family member?
faqs.a: Yes, and most people do. Say in the booking who the visit is for and how to reach them, and tell them a helper is coming — arriving unannounced at an older person's door is nobody's idea of help.

faqs.q: What activities are included?
faqs.a: Conversation, a walk, a grocery trip, light housekeeping, help with post and forms, company for an outing. {base} covers the first {inclTime}, with {blockPrice} per extra {blockTime}.

faqs.q: Can a helper accompany an appointment?
faqs.a: They can go along and be company, carry things, and take notes if asked. They cannot speak for the person, consent to treatment, or make a decision on anyone's behalf.

faqs.q: What accessibility details should I share?
faqs.a: All of them, in the booking: stairs, mobility aids, hearing, memory, language, anything that shapes how the visit should go. A helper who knows before accepting is a helper who can actually help.

faqs.q: Can the same helper come back?
faqs.a: Yes, and for this service it matters more than most. Save them as a favourite and send future requests to them first, so visits are from a familiar face rather than a new one each time.

page.title: Errand Runner — Hire Help With Everyday Errands | Helpward
page.h1: Hire someone to run your errands
page.intro: The list of small things that each take twenty minutes and together take an afternoon. On Helpward this is the Errand Runner service: write the tasks and the stops in order, set a spending limit if money is involved, and a helper works through them.

faqs.q: Which errands can I request?
faqs.a: Anything lawful that a person on foot or in a car can do for you: collections, drop-offs, posting things, picking things up, queueing at a counter. The form takes one task per line, and the stops in the order they should happen.

faqs.q: Can a helper shop for items?
faqs.a: Yes — set a spending limit on the form and the helper buys within it. If what you want is a grocery order you have already placed and paid for, Grocery Pickup is the better fit; if it is one parcel going one place, use Package Delivery.

faqs.q: How are purchases paid for?
faqs.a: Separately from the booking fee, and the spending limit is the control: it is the number a helper is not meant to exceed. Keep receipts in the conversation so what was bought and what it cost are both on the record.

faqs.q: Can I add multiple stops?
faqs.a: Yes, and the form asks for them in order. More stops means more time, and time beyond the first hour is what moves the price.

faqs.q: How do I share handover instructions?
faqs.a: In the handover instructions on the booking — gate codes, which buzzer, where to leave things. They are saved with the booking and readable only by the helper actually booked, not by every helper the request was offered to.

faqs.q: Is waiting time included?
faqs.a: It is part of the booked time, so yes, within it. {base} covers the first {inclTime} and each extra {blockTime} is {blockPrice} — a queue you expect to be long is worth booking time for up front.

includes: The tasks and stops you list, in order
Buying items within a spending limit you set
Waiting time, within the time you book

excludes: Anything unlawful, or age-restricted without you present

page.title: Furniture Assembly — IKEA & Flat-Pack Help | Helpward
page.h1: Book help assembling your furniture
page.intro: The flat-pack box you have been stepping around for a fortnight, built. On Helpward this is the Furniture Assembly service: say what the items are and how many, and the helper works through them in the time you book.

faqs.q: Can you assemble IKEA furniture?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the most common request. Any flat-pack furniture with its own instructions and fittings is the same job — the brand matters less than whether all the parts are in the box.

faqs.q: What item details should I provide?
faqs.a: What the items are and how many. A product name or model is worth adding: "two Malm drawer units" tells a helper what they are walking into, and "furniture" does not.

faqs.q: Does the helper bring tools?
faqs.a: The form asks whether tools are needed, so answer it. Most flat-pack packs include the Allen key that builds them; a power driver is a different matter and worth flagging.

faqs.q: Is wall anchoring included?
faqs.a: Only where it is straightforward and you have the fixings. Anything that means drilling into an unknown wall, or load-bearing fixing you would want certified, is outside an assembly booking — say what you need on the form so a helper can judge it before accepting.

faqs.q: Do you remove the packaging?
faqs.a: The form asks whether you want the packaging dealt with, and the helper can break it down and take it out. Disposal beyond your own bins is not part of it.

faqs.q: How is it priced?
faqs.a: {base} covers the first {inclTime}, then {blockPrice} per extra {blockTime}. Item count drives how much time to book rather than adding a separate charge, so the total you see is the total.

page.title: Sleep Call Companion — Quiet Audio Company | Helpward
page.h1: Book quiet audio company while you fall asleep
page.intro: A quiet voice on a call while you fall asleep, for an agreed stretch of time. On Helpward this is the Sleep Call Companion service: audio only, as much or as little conversation as you want, and a definite end time set when you book.

faqs.q: How long does the call last?
faqs.a: As long as you booked, and no longer. {base} covers the first {inclTime}, with {blockPrice} per extra {blockTime}. There is no open-ended or all-night call — the end time is fixed before it starts.

faqs.q: Is this audio only?
faqs.a: Yes. No video, and nobody comes to you.

faqs.q: What happens when I fall asleep?
faqs.a: The helper stays on for the time you booked and then ends the call. That is what the agreed end time is for — it means nobody has to decide anything while you are asleep.

faqs.q: Can I choose quiet company instead of conversation?
faqs.a: Yes, and plenty of people do. Say which you want when you book, so the helper knows whether they are talking or just there.

faqs.q: Is the call recorded?
faqs.a: Not by Helpward, and no one on the call should be recording it.

faqs.q: Is this a treatment for insomnia?
faqs.a: No. It is company, not medicine. It makes no claim to treat insomnia, anxiety or any condition, and persistent sleep trouble is worth raising with a doctor.

faqs.q: Do I need to supply a bracket?
faqs.a: Yes, and the form asks which one you have. A mount has to match both the television and the wall, so it is the one thing worth buying before you book rather than after.

faqs.q: Which wall types are supported?

faqs.q: Can you mount a large TV?

faqs.q: Is cable concealment included?

faqs.q: What details affect the quote?

row.blurb: A helper waits in an eligible queue for as long as you book, then hands their place to you where the venue allows it. You are paying for their time — admission, stock and appointments are not guaranteed.

page.title: Hire Someone to Wait in Line — Line Sitter Service | Helpward
page.h1: Pay someone to wait in an eligible line for you
page.intro: Spend someone else's hours in the queue instead of your own. On Helpward this is the Wait in Line service: a helper holds a place for as long as you book, then hands it over where the venue allows it. You are paying for their time — not for admission, a ticket, or whatever is at the front.

faqs.q: Can someone hold my place at this venue?
faqs.a: That is the venue's call, and you should check before you book. Plenty of queues allow it; ticketed events, government offices and anything requiring the named person to be present usually do not. Helpward cannot overrule a venue's rules and does not promise it can.

faqs.q: How do we hand over the place?
faqs.a: You meet the helper in the queue and take their spot. Agree a meeting point in the booking and stay in touch as the line moves, because the handover is the part that needs timing.

faqs.q: What if the helper reaches the front first?
faqs.a: Then the booking has run out of usefulness unless you are there. A helper cannot buy, enter, register or sign on your behalf — plan to arrive before the front, and extend the booking if the queue moves slower than you thought.

faqs.q: Can I extend the waiting time?
faqs.a: Yes. {base} covers the first {inclTime} and each extra {blockTime} is {blockPrice}. Arrange it with the helper through the booking — their time is theirs, so an extension is an agreement rather than something you can impose.

faqs.q: Are tickets or purchases included?
faqs.a: No. Nothing is bought on your behalf and nothing at the front of the line is included. You are buying someone's hours standing still.

faqs.q: What if the venue refuses the handover?
faqs.a: Then the place is lost, and no one can promise otherwise. This is the real risk of the service, which is why checking the venue's policy first is worth more than anything we could write here.

faqs.q: Can I book more than one guest?

faqs.q: Are meals and venue access included?

faqs.q: Does the venue need to know?
faqs.a: You should assume yes. It is your event and your relationship with the venue; Helpward is supplying attendance, not permission.

faqs.q: How is time and guest count priced?
faqs.a: Per person, by time booked. Each guest is their own booking with its own hours, so the total is simply the sum of them, each shown in full before you send it.

faqs.q: How does this differ from an event companion?
faqs.a: An Event Companion goes with you to someone else's event. This fills seats at yours. Different job, different briefing.
